plain_english_title: Wartime Pension Net Worth, Financial Competency Due Process & Overpayment Waiver Snapshots
what_this_means: This module compiles the exact regulations governing three critical protections for wartime Veterans and Survivors: (1) VA Pension net-worth limits, deductible assisted-living/medical expenses, and the 36-month asset-transfer lookback enacted October 18, 2018 (38 C.F.R. §§ 3.272(g) and 3.274–3.279, published September 18, 2018 at 83 FR 47246), (2) strict due-process protections before VA can declare a beneficiary unable to manage their own VA funds and appoint a fiduciary (38 C.F.R. §§ 3.353 and 3.105(h)–(i)), and (3) requesting an 'equity and good conscience' waiver of a VA benefit overpayment within the 1-year deadline (38 C.F.R. §§ 1.963 and 1.965).
record_clues: VA Form 21P-527EZ (Veterans Pension), VA Form 21P-534EZ (Survivors Pension), or VA Form 21P-8416 (Medical Expense Report) showing nursing-home, assisted-living, memory-care, or in-home care expenses offsetting countable income.
A VA Pension denial penalizing an asset gift or transfer made BEFORE October 18, 2018, or penalizing a transfer when total net worth never exceeded VA's bright-line limit.

A proposed financial incompetency letter or C&P mental health checkbox stating the Veteran cannot manage financial affairs (triggering 60-day response and predetermination hearing rights under 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.353 and 3.105(h)–(i)).

A Debt Management Center (DMC) Notice of Indebtedness and VA Form 5655 (Financial Status Report)—especially if VA rejected a waiver request filed between Day 181 and Day 365 on a post-December 29, 2022 debt letter.
important_cautions: October 18, 2018 Pension transfer cutoff: VA's 36-month lookback penalty (38 C.F.R. § 3.276) applies ONLY to uncompensated transfers of 'covered assets' (assets above the net-worth cap) made ON OR AFTER October 18, 2018—transfers completed before October 18, 2018 must be disregarded under § 3.276(b), and primary residences up to a 2-acre marketable lot remain excluded under § 3.275.

Expanded 1-year debt waiver deadline: Congress expanded the statutory overpayment waiver deadline from 180 days to 1 full year effective December 29, 2022 (Pub. L. 117-328, Div. U, § 254; 38 U.S.C. § 5302(a)), even though VA did not update 38 C.F.R. § 1.963(b) until January 26, 2026 (published November 26, 2025 at 90 FR 54234). Note also that requesting a waiver or dispute within 30 days of the First Demand Letter freezes monthly benefit withholding while VA reviews the request.

Fraud, misrepresentation, or bad faith is an absolute bar to an equitable waiver under 38 U.S.C. § 5302(c) and 38 C.F.R. § 1.965(b), and contesting whether the debt is legally valid at all is separate from asking for a waiver.

Competency benefit-of-the-doubt rule: under 38 C.F.R. § 3.353(c)–(e), VA cannot finalize an incompetency finding without advance notice, an opportunity for a hearing, and resolving any reasonable doubt in favor of competency.
questions_for_representative: In calculating my VA Pension or Aid and Attendance eligibility, did VA deduct all qualifying unreimbursed assisted-living, memory-care, or in-home care expenses exceeding 5% of the base pension rate under 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.272(g) and 3.278?

If I received a Debt Management Center overpayment notice, can we both contest the validity of the underlying debt (for example, sole VA administrative error under 38 U.S.C. § 5112(b)(10)) AND file a protective waiver request within 30 days (to pause withholding) and within the 1-year deadline?
Was my waiver request wrongly dismissed as 'untimely' between December 29, 2022 and January 26, 2026 because VA staff applied the outdated 180-day regulation instead of the 1-year statute?

If VA proposed to rate me incompetent to handle my VA funds, how do we request a predetermination hearing within 30 days and submit lay or medical evidence showing I manage my bills (or with assistance)?
